title: 5 must-watch movies & TV shows streaming right now
author: Kevin Slane
bullets: 'The Devil Wears Prada 2' featuring Meryl Streep is streaming on Hulu, focusing on print media challenges.
'The Drama', a dark comedy with Zendaya and Robert Pattinson, is available on HBO Max.
'Furious' Season 1 with Emmy Rossum, a crime series on Hulu, portrays an FBI agent tracking a serial killer.

title: Here’s how home, away broadcasts reacted to Jarren Duran’s on-field flare-up
author: Kaley Brown
bullets: Jarren Duran stirred controversy by criticizing teammate Willson Contreras and third base coach Chad Epperson during a game.
NESN and WEEI broadcasts criticized Duran's public outburst, noting Contreras wouldn't have scored on the fly ball.
The Red Sox are open to trading Duran before MLB's trade deadline after his on-field incident.

title: Drake Maye on building chemistry with A.J. Brown: ‘I am not going to shy away from him.’
author: Khari A. Thompson
bullets: Drake Maye and A.J. Brown are building chemistry during Patriots training camp in Foxborough.
Maye completed all but one pass during Friday's team drills, connecting frequently with Brown.
The Patriots are six practices into training camp, focusing on improving quarterback-receiver communication.

title: Drake Maye, A.J. Brown heat up and other takeaways from Day 6 of Patriots training camp
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Drake Maye completed 18-of-19 passes in team drills since padded practices began, including a perfect 11-for-11 on Friday.
A.J. Brown, the Patriots' top offseason pickup, recorded multiple catches from quarterback Drake Maye during team drills.
Romeo Doubs made the top play of practice with a touchdown catch in the red zone over star defender Christian Gonzalez.

title: Massachusetts falls out of top 10 in best state rankings by U.S. News & World Report
author: Annie Jonas
bullets: Massachusetts ranked No. 11 in U.S. News & World Report's 2026 Best States rankings, down from No. 9 in 2025.
The state excelled in health care, ranking second, but faced challenges in fiscal stability (39th) and infrastructure (38th).
Utah retained the overall top spot, followed by South Dakota and Minnesota; New Hampshire ranked sixth, down from second.

title: Massachusetts loses two IHOP restaurants
author: Beth Treffeisen
bullets: IHOP closed its Cambridge and Hyannis locations, reducing the number of Massachusetts restaurants to 19.
The closures may result from low foot traffic or expired leases and sparked nostalgia among Cape Cod locals.
IHOP, owned by Dine Brands Global, still operates 1,812 franchised locations and 12 company stores worldwide.

title: Court agrees Wu did not discriminate against North End restaurants, but may have illegally taxed them
author: Abby Patkin
bullets: The U.S. First Circuit Court upheld the dismissal of a lawsuit against Boston's outdoor dining policy by North End restaurants.
Boston Mayor Michelle Wu's administration was cleared of discrimination claims related to the pandemic-era outdoor dining regulations.
Restaurants can potentially challenge the 2022 outdoor dining fees as unlawful taxes after the court's partial ruling.

title: MassDOT releases rendering of two new bridges along McGrath Highway
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: MassDOT plans two new bridges on McGrath Highway, set for McGrath Boulevard transition.
The replacement will include Squires Bridge and a new Somerville Avenue Extension Bridge.
Construction, starting possibly in 2030, aims to improve connectivity and safety in Somerville/Cambridge.

title: ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ review: Peter Parker grows up in emotionally mature sequel
author: Kevin Slane
bullets: 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' features Tom Holland as Peter Parker dealing with personal struggles and isolation.
Director Destin Daniel Cretton's film presents a more emotionally mature approach, with a grayer depiction of New York City.
Zendaya shines as MJ, given a larger role in the narrative, alongside Peter's battle with a faceless villain.

title: This Boston law firm is boosting starting salaries to $235,000
author: Beth Treffeisen
bullets: McDermott Will & Schulte LLP increased starting salaries for first-year associates to $235,000, effective July 1.
This increase aligns McDermott with top U.S. firms like Milbank, which also offer $235,000 base salaries.
Despite Boston's large legal market, no other major city firms have publicly matched McDermott's new salary.
